newsitem.title: ESTONIA: BALTIC CRESCO EXPECTS MORE STOCK MARKET GAINS.
newsitem.headline: BALTIC CRESCO EXPECTS MORE STOCK MARKET GAINS.

text.p: Estonia's Baltic Cresco investment house said it expected the general rise of the Tallinn stock market to continue.
"There has already been a good rise and this will continue," Andres Ratsepp, Cresco chief executive, told Reuters.
"Stocks are not over-valued and their prices are supported by good financial reports," he told Reuters in a recent interview. "We are very positive about the market.

Baltic Cresco operates like a investment bank and is not concerned about competition with Talinvest, which Ratsepp says is more like a merchant bank and relies on its own capital for investment projects.
"Our strategies are very different and our strength lies in our sales networks,"
"For example during the successful Pennu share issue we used the sales network of the Swedish Enskilda Securities," he added.
The investment company has several projects due for completion in May in Estonia.
Ratsepp said Cresco is working on two new share issues in Estonia -- the Nissan car retailer, Fakto, and the share issue for Estiko, both of which will begin in April.
"We are also part part of a consortium for the purchase of the Estonian Shipping company," he said.
The sale of the Estonian shipping company will be reviewed again in late May, according to officials from the privatisation agency.
